review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib for other pseudoelement or PseudoEqual constructions. Only Subobject/Basic.lean and Abelian/Refinements.lean mention them. Refinements.lean is a different, complementary diagram-chasing tool, not a competing definition of the same concept. The one candidate was `app f a := a.hom ≫ f`, which overlaps with `(Over.map f).obj a`. Its docstring says the choice is deliberate, for nicer definitional properties. The rubric says a named API implemented via a generic map is not redundant, and `app` has only about three uses. I did not find that it duplicates substantive API or forces repeated conversions. `PseudoEqual`, `Pseudoelement` and `pseudoApply` have no Mathlib counterpart: a quotient of `Over P` by pseudo-equality is not `Subobject P`. The `Std.Refl`/`Std.Symm`/`IsTrans` instances and the `Setoid` use existing core and Mathlib classes. I found no justified finding.
